node.title: When a regexp with /g needs to be run .. twice
node.author: talexb
node.doctext:
This is interesting (to me). I'm cleaning up some JSON so that it's palatable to the API I'm using, and I'm discovering some unexpected behaviour. $foo = ':{"' $foo =~ s/([:,{])(.)/$1 $2/g; print "'$foo'\n"; I'm expecting this regexp to insert spaces after all occurrences of left square bracket, colon and left brace. The result: ': {"' If I run the regexp again, I finally get the result I'm expecting: ': { "' That's counter-intuitive to me .. if I put 'g' at the end of a regexp, I expect it to run that expression repeatedly (flashback to COBOL .. REPEAT UNTIL DONE).

Thoughts?

Alex / [talexb] / Toronto

Thanks PJ. We owe you so much. Groklaw -- RIP -- 2003 to 2013.
